# Full Stack Web Development syllabus

<!-- Generated by `node scripts/build.mjs` from curriculum.json. Edit curriculum.json, not this file. -->

31 lessons over 11 weeks at 5 sessions a week. Most lessons take one session. Lessons marked **Project** take several sessions and end with a larger build that you submit as its own pull request.

Stack: HTML, CSS, JavaScript, TypeScript, Node.js, Express, PostgreSQL, React, Vitest, Playwright, GitHub Actions.

## Getting started

### 00. Orientation and dev environment

Week 1. Folder [`lessons/00-orientation`](lessons/00-orientation).

You will be able to:

- Install Node.js, Git, VS Code, and the GitHub CLI
- Move around the file system from the terminal
- Clone your course repo and run its tests

Exercises:

- Install the toolchain and save its version output for your lesson 01 pull request

### 01. Git and GitHub: commits, branches, pull requests

Week 1. Folder [`lessons/01-git-and-github`](lessons/01-git-and-github).

You will be able to:

- Explain what a commit, a branch, and a remote are
- Create a branch, commit, push, and open a pull request
- Respond to review comments with new commits

Exercises:

- Write an `about-me.md` and submit it as your first pull request
- Fix the review comment your instructor leaves on it

## Web foundations

### 02. How the web works

Week 1. Folder [`lessons/02-how-the-web-works`](lessons/02-how-the-web-works).

You will be able to:

- Trace a request from URL to rendered page: DNS, TCP, HTTP, HTML
- Read requests and responses in the browser Network tab
- Name the common HTTP methods and status codes

Exercises:

- Use `curl -v` on three sites and annotate the request and response headers
- Answer the HTTP status code quiz

### 03. Semantic HTML and accessibility

Week 1. Folder [`lessons/03-html`](lessons/03-html).

You will be able to:

- Structure a page with semantic elements
- Build an accessible form with labels and validation attributes
- Check a page with the browser accessibility tree

Exercises:

- Mark up a recipe page from a plain-text recipe
- Build a sign-up form that passes the accessibility checklist

### 04. CSS fundamentals

Week 1. Folder [`lessons/04-css-fundamentals`](lessons/04-css-fundamentals).

You will be able to:

- Apply selectors, specificity, and the cascade
- Size elements with the box model
- Use custom properties for colors and spacing

Exercises:

- Style the recipe page from lesson 03
- Fix the five specificity bugs in `broken.css`

### 05. CSS layout: flexbox, grid, responsive design

Week 2. Folder [`lessons/05-css-layout`](lessons/05-css-layout).

You will be able to:

- Lay out components with flexbox
- Lay out pages with grid
- Make a page work from 320px to 1440px with media queries

Exercises:

- Rebuild three layouts from screenshots
- Project 1: personal portfolio site

## JavaScript

### 06. JavaScript basics

Week 2. Folder [`lessons/06-js-basics`](lessons/06-js-basics).

You will be able to:

- Use values, variables, and operators
- Control flow with conditionals and loops
- Write and call functions that return values

Exercises:

- Temperature converter
- FizzBuzz
- Password strength checker

### 07. Arrays and objects

Week 2. Folder [`lessons/07-arrays-and-objects`](lessons/07-arrays-and-objects).

You will be able to:

- Model data with arrays and objects
- Transform data with map, filter, and reduce
- Copy and compare objects without mutation bugs

Exercises:

- Gradebook statistics
- Shopping cart totals
- Group transactions by category

### 08. Functions, scope, and closures

Week 3. Folder [`lessons/08-functions-and-scope`](lessons/08-functions-and-scope).

You will be able to:

- Predict what a variable refers to in nested scopes
- Write higher-order functions
- Use closures to keep private state

Exercises:

- Write `once`, `memoize`, and `debounce`
- Build a counter factory

### 09. The DOM and events

Week 3. Folder [`lessons/09-dom-and-events`](lessons/09-dom-and-events).

You will be able to:

- Select, create, and update elements
- Handle clicks, input, and form submission
- Keep the UI in sync with a single state object

Exercises:

- To-do list with add, complete, and delete
- Filterable product list

### 10. Asynchronous JavaScript and fetch

Week 3. Folder [`lessons/10-async-and-fetch`](lessons/10-async-and-fetch).

You will be able to:

- Explain the event loop at a whiteboard level
- Use promises and async/await
- Fetch JSON from an API and handle loading and error states

Exercises:

- Weather widget backed by a public API
- Retry a failing request with backoff

### 11. Modules, npm, and testing

Week 3-4. Folder [`lessons/11-tooling-and-testing`](lessons/11-tooling-and-testing).

You will be able to:

- Split code into ES modules
- Install and run packages with npm
- Write unit tests with Vitest

Exercises:

- Write tests for an untested utility module
- Project 2: interactive quiz app with a test suite

## Back end

### 12. Node.js fundamentals

Week 4. Folder [`lessons/12-node-fundamentals`](lessons/12-node-fundamentals).

You will be able to:

- Run JavaScript outside the browser
- Read and write files, and read environment variables
- Build a small command-line tool

Exercises:

- Word-count CLI
- CSV-to-JSON converter

### 13. HTTP servers with Express

Week 4. Folder [`lessons/13-express`](lessons/13-express).

You will be able to:

- Create routes for each HTTP method
- Write and order middleware
- Serve static files and JSON

Exercises:

- Notes API with in-memory storage
- Request-logging middleware

### 14. REST API design, validation, and errors

Week 4. Folder [`lessons/14-rest-api-design`](lessons/14-rest-api-design).

You will be able to:

- Design resource URLs and pick status codes
- Validate request bodies at the boundary
- Return consistent error responses

Exercises:

- Add validation and error handling to the Notes API
- Write integration tests with Supertest

## Databases

### 15. SQL with PostgreSQL

Week 4. Folder [`lessons/15-sql`](lessons/15-sql).

You will be able to:

- Create tables and insert, update, and delete rows
- Query with WHERE, ORDER BY, GROUP BY, and JOIN
- Explain primary keys and foreign keys

Exercises:

- Twenty query challenges on a bookstore database

### 16. Data modeling and migrations

Week 5. Folder [`lessons/16-data-modeling`](lessons/16-data-modeling).

You will be able to:

- Model one-to-many and many-to-many relationships
- Write and run migrations
- Choose constraints that block bad data

Exercises:

- Design the schema for a library app
- Write migrations for it

### 17. Connecting Node to PostgreSQL

Week 5. Folder [`lessons/17-node-and-postgres`](lessons/17-node-and-postgres).

You will be able to:

- Query Postgres from Node with parameterized queries
- Explain and prevent SQL injection
- Use transactions

Exercises:

- Move the Notes API from memory to Postgres
- Project 3: REST API for the library app

## TypeScript

### 18. TypeScript basics

Week 5. Folder [`lessons/18-typescript-basics`](lessons/18-typescript-basics).

You will be able to:

- Annotate variables, functions, and objects
- Read and fix compiler errors
- Convert a JavaScript module to TypeScript

Exercises:

- Convert the lesson 07 exercises to TypeScript

### 19. TypeScript in practice

Week 6. Folder [`lessons/19-typescript-in-practice`](lessons/19-typescript-in-practice).

You will be able to:

- Model data with union types
- Write generic functions
- Parse untrusted input with Zod

Exercises:

- Type the library API end to end
- Model an order lifecycle with a discriminated union

## Front end with React

### 20. React components and JSX

Week 6. Folder [`lessons/20-react-components`](lessons/20-react-components).

You will be able to:

- Build components that take props
- Render lists and conditional UI
- Set up a project with Vite

Exercises:

- Rebuild the product list from lesson 09 in React

### 21. State and effects

Week 6. Folder [`lessons/21-react-state`](lessons/21-react-state).

You will be able to:

- Manage state with useState
- Lift state up and pass callbacks down
- Use useEffect only for syncing with outside systems

Exercises:

- To-do app in React
- Find the bugs in three misused effects

### 22. Forms and data fetching

Week 6. Folder [`lessons/22-react-forms-and-data`](lessons/22-react-forms-and-data).

You will be able to:

- Build controlled forms with validation messages
- Fetch from your own API with loading and error states
- Test components with Testing Library

Exercises:

- Library app front end: list and add books

### 23. Routing and app structure

Week 6. Folder [`lessons/23-react-routing`](lessons/23-react-routing).

You will be able to:

- Add client-side routes
- Organize a growing React codebase by feature
- Share state across routes

Exercises:

- Add book detail and edit pages to the library app

## Full stack

### 24. Authentication and sessions

Week 7. Folder [`lessons/24-authentication`](lessons/24-authentication).

You will be able to:

- Hash passwords
- Log users in with cookie sessions
- Protect routes on the server and the client

Exercises:

- Add sign-up, log-in, and log-out to the library app

### 25. Web security basics

Week 7. Folder [`lessons/25-web-security`](lessons/25-web-security).

You will be able to:

- Prevent XSS, CSRF, and SQL injection
- Configure CORS correctly
- Keep secrets out of Git

Exercises:

- Find and fix the six vulnerabilities in the sample app

### 26. Testing across the stack

Week 7. Folder [`lessons/26-testing-the-stack`](lessons/26-testing-the-stack).

You will be able to:

- Choose between unit, integration, and end-to-end tests
- Write end-to-end tests with Playwright
- Run tests in GitHub Actions

Exercises:

- Add Playwright tests for log-in and adding a book
- Project 4: full-stack library app

## Shipping

### 27. Deployment and CI/CD

Week 8. Folder [`lessons/27-deployment`](lessons/27-deployment).

You will be able to:

- Build for production and configure environment variables
- Deploy a front end, an API, and a database
- Deploy automatically when main changes

Exercises:

- Deploy the library app and post the live URL in your PR

### 28. Debugging and performance in production

Week 8. Folder [`lessons/28-debugging-production`](lessons/28-debugging-production).

You will be able to:

- Read logs and stack traces from a deployed app
- Find slow queries and add indexes
- Measure page performance with Lighthouse

Exercises:

- Diagnose the three planted bugs in the deployed sample app

## Career

### 29. Working on a team

Week 8. Folder [`lessons/29-working-on-a-team`](lessons/29-working-on-a-team).

You will be able to:

- Write clear issues and pull request descriptions
- Give and receive code review
- Work in an existing codebase you did not write

Exercises:

- Review two classmates' pull requests
- Fix a labeled issue in the class open-source repo

### 30. Capstone project and job search

Week 8-11. Folder [`lessons/30-capstone`](lessons/30-capstone).

You will be able to:

- Plan, build, and ship an app of your own design
- Present your project and explain its trade-offs
- Prepare your portfolio, resume, and GitHub profile

Exercises:

- Capstone: a full-stack app you design, shipped over three weeks with one PR per milestone
